page: Microsoft Azure D160ads_v7 is a high-capacity instance from the Dadsv7 family, powered by an AMD EPYC 9V45 processor. It features 160 vCPUs mapped to 80 physical cores with multithreading enabled, operating at a clock speed of 4.5 GHz. The system is equipped with 640 GB of system memory, yielding a balanced 4 GB of RAM per vCPU. Storage is bundled as a 9449 GB local disk, and the instance is capable of utilizing Premium Storage. It runs on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor using the x86_64 architecture.

Benchmark data places this instance in the top tier for both single-core and multi-core CPU performance via stress-ng and Geekbench. Memory bandwidth is highly efficient, reaching 14521.33 GB/sec for cached small-block reads and 464.15 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads. The CPU architecture supports advanced vector instructions including AVX-512 and AVX_VNNI, which contribute to top-tier performance in cryptographic operations, database transactions, and software compilation. LLM inference benchmarks show strong to top-tier capabilities, processing up to 6166.69 tokens per second on small models and maintaining 8.92 tokens per second for text generation on large 70B models.

From a resource density perspective, the D160ads_v7 offers high qualitative cost efficiency for large-scale deployments by consolidating massive compute, memory, and local storage into a single virtual machine. This high-tier hardware class minimizes the overhead associated with multi-node orchestration. However, a notable tradeoff is the absence of dedicated GPU hardware, meaning highly parallelized deep learning training workloads must rely on CPU execution or be routed to GPU-accelerated families.

This instance is optimized for demanding enterprise workloads. It is highly suited for large-scale relational and non-relational databases, high-throughput web serving, heavy software compilation pipelines, and data compression tasks. Additionally, the combination of 160 vCPUs and 640 GB of RAM makes it an excellent fit for CPU-based machine learning inference, large-scale simulation, and complex ETL data processing.
description: The Microsoft Azure D160ads_v7 is a high-capacity, general-purpose instance from the Dadsv7 family, powered by an AMD EPYC 9V45 processor. It features 160 vCPUs running at 4.5 GHz, paired with 640 GB of RAM and a substantial 9449 GB local storage disk. Operating on the x86_64 architecture under Microsoft Hyper-V, the instance delivers top-tier performance, placing in the top 10% of benchmarks for multi-core CPU execution, memory bandwidth, and database operations. While it lacks a dedicated GPU, its high resource density and advanced vector extensions make it highly cost-efficient for consolidating massive workloads. The D160ads_v7 is best suited for large-scale databases, high-throughput web serving, software compilation, and CPU-based LLM inference.
